statement: Opportunity Zone designation authority was granted by the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017, codified in IRC section 1400Z-2.
Governors and chief executives nominate eligible low-income census tracts; the U.S. Treasury certifies and designates them.

First-round designations were announced April 9, 2018 (18 states); the final round June 14, 2018 (all 50 states, DC, 5 territories). Adjudicated tract count: 8,764 (IRS Notice 2018-48); r1's 8,761 is a superseded early figure.
Eligible tracts are (1) low-income communities or (2) non-LIC contiguous tracts, the latter limited to 25% of a state's eligible LIC tracts.
GAO found selected tracts had higher poverty and a greater share of non-White populations than eligible-but-unselected tracts; differences statistically significant.
forbidden_inference: Descriptive statistical comparison only. The statute targets low-income tracts by design; must NOT be read as intentional racial targeting, investor self-dealing, or misconduct. Verified verbatim against GAO-22-104019.

statement: GAO found no single agency was designated to collect comprehensive OZ performance and tax-compliance data.
As of 2019, more than 6,000 Qualified Opportunity Funds had invested approximately $29 billion, per partial IRS data (directional aggregate; no entity-level or temporal resolution).
Under 1400Z-2, investors may defer gain by investing in a QOF within 180 days, with exclusion tiers at 5-, 7-, and 10-year holds.
